A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TR scheduling work and contain 19 readable pages, including supplementary Sections S1-S5. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-classification and object-detection experiments in Tables 1-4, alongside supplementary experiments, ablations, and training analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original classification, detection, and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: The TR computation, running average, TALR update, quantization schemes, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The supplementary alternative update schemes are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet and CIFAR-10/100 for classification and MS COCO for object detection. No dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main optimizer comparisons, Table S5's additional optimizers, and Table S1's QAT comparisons, including LSQ, LSQ+, EWGS, and Nagel et al.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1 and S4.1 and Table S8 retain the same splits, metrics, architectures, bit-widths, training budgets, and scheduler settings. Corrected section references do not change the experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Sections S2-S3 retain the analyses of TR dynamics, scheduler choice, initial and final TRs, optimizer choice, and TALR update variants. The object-detection case studies in Figure S2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table S6 and Section S3.1 report means and standard deviations over five random runs in both versions. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: The main and supplementary result tables and graphics retain their values and findings. For example, Table 1's MobileNetV2 W2A2 SGD/SGDT accuracies remain 46.9/53.6, and Table 4's ResNet-50 W4A4 AP values remain 38.05/38.36.

T1.justification: The definitions, derivations, and equations in the main text and supplement are unchanged, including the negligible post-scaling change and single-transition assumptions underlying Equation (9).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that conventional LR scheduling is suboptimal for QAT and that TR scheduling improves training stability and performance across architectures, optimizers, and tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning weight oscillation, concentration near transition points, and aggressive quantization are unchanged. Qualifications about extreme TR factors in Section S2.3 and layer-specific target selection in Section S3.3 are also retained.

D1.justification: v3's abstract promises future online code availability; v4 removes that sentence and supplies a specific project-page link beneath the authors. This adds access information, although the PDFs do not establish whether code is available there. Implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 50 cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to citation page backreferences reflect document reflow rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: v4 corrects a spelling error and Section 5's overview references, changes the detection discussion's Table S2 references to Table 4, and directs Section 5.3 to Figure 3 instead of Figure S3. It also updates one affiliation and adds funding acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The title block is reformatted, Table 3 moves from the right to the left column on page 7, and acknowledgements cause reference-page reflow. Figures, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves navigation by correcting internal references, particularly directing the ResNet-50 detection discussion to the appropriate Table 4 rather than Table S2. The project-page link also improves resource discoverability. These are limited improvements in usability; the scientific methods, results, and supporting evidence remain unchanged.
